title: Non-vacuity witness Φ₀ stipulates the warrant it should derive (circular 𝓙_Φ)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
In Proposition 1 (Non-vacuity), the single postulate P of 𝓜₀ *stipulates* that 'the avowed update rule is conditionalisation' and that the aim is coherence. The (O2) step then 'proves' Π_c (conditionalisation) is warranted essentially because P avows it. This makes the justificatory derivation ⊢_Φ 'Π_c is warranted' trivial: the warrant was placed in 𝓜₀ by hand. The solution is candid about this but candor does not close the gap.

Consequence: if a framework may simply postulate the warrant of any procedure, then 𝓙_Φ and 𝓞_Φ are inhabited for *any* procedure under a suitably crafted Φ, draining (O2)/𝓙_Φ of content and undermining Proposition (b)'s claim that quid juris? is 'answerable' rather than question-begging. The non-vacuity proof is thus circular relative to the very notion (𝓙_Φ) it inhabits.

Fix: make 𝓜₀ contain the *aim* (minimise expected inaccuracy / coherence axioms), NOT the rule, and *derive* the warrant of conditionalisation by an agent-invariant L-proof from an accuracy-dominance theorem (Greaves–Wallace 2006; Pettigrew, Accuracy and the Laws of Credence) or a Dutch-book argument. Then (O2) is a real derivation, honoring the preface's refusal to solve Hume while still earning the witness.
